questions.question: Sami calls Mina in an emergency: 'A patient has blisters on the gum and mucosa!' Mina replies: 'It could be pemphigus.' What is pemphigus vulgaris?
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Pemphigus is a severe autoimmune disease.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will refer the patient urgently.'

questions.question: Sami wonders: 'How to differentiate pemphigus from pemphigoid?' Mina replies:
options: Pemphigus has fragile intraepithelial blisters, pemphigoid is subepithelial
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'The difference is histological.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will request a biopsy to confirm.'

questions.question: Sami asks: 'Why is pemphigus an emergency?' Mina replies:
options: It can be fatal without treatment, with malnutrition and infections
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Pemphigus can be life-threatening.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will hospitalize the patient.'

questions.question: Sami wonders: 'How is pemphigus treated?' Mina replies:
options: Systemic corticosteroids and immunosuppressants, with specialist follow-up
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Treatment requires specialized management.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will refer to a dermatologist.'

questions.question: Sami asks: 'What is Sjögren's syndrome?' Mina replies:
options: An autoimmune disease affecting the salivary and lacrimal glands
A bacterial infection of the salivary glands
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Sjögren's is an autoimmune disease.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will look for signs of xerostomia.'

questions.question: Sami wonders: 'What are the oral risks of Sjögren's?' Mina replies:
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Sjögren's exposes to many oral complications.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will recommend regular monitoring.'

questions.question: Sami asks: 'What is trigeminal neuralgia?' Mina replies:
options: Brief, intense, paroxysmal pain, triggered by a stimulus
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Trigeminal neuralgia is characteristic.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will recognize it.'

questions.question: Sami wonders: 'How is trigeminal neuralgia treated?' Mina replies:
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Treatment is medical, sometimes surgical.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will refer to a neurologist.'

questions.question: Sami asks: 'What is TMD (temporomandibular dysfunction)?' Mina replies:
options: A painful syndrome of the temporomandibular joint
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'TMD is a painful syndrome of the TMJ.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will look for the signs.'

questions.question: Sami wonders: 'How is TMD treated?' Mina replies:
options: Physiotherapy, occlusal splint, analgesics, stress management
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Treatment is often conservative.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will propose a splint.'

questions.question: Sami asks: 'What is desquamative gingivitis?' Mina replies:
options: Desquamation of the gum, often associated with lichen planus or pemphigoid
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'It's often a sign of an autoimmune disease.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will do a workup.'

questions.question: Sami wonders: 'How is desquamative gingivitis treated?' Mina replies:
options: Treatment of the underlying disease, topical corticosteroids
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Treatment targets the underlying cause.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will refer to a specialist.'

questions.question: Sami asks: 'What is drug-induced stomatitis?' Mina replies:
options: An inflammatory reaction of the mucosa to a medication
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Drug-induced stomatitis is a reaction to a medication.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will ask the patient about their medications.'

questions.question: Sami wonders: 'Which medications can cause stomatitis?' Mina replies:
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Many medications can cause stomatitis.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will look for the medication in question.'

questions.question: Sami asks: 'What is xerostomia?' Mina replies:
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Xerostomia is dry mouth.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will look for the causes.'

questions.question: Sami wonders: 'What are the causes of xerostomia?' Mina replies:
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'The causes are numerous.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will look for the cause.'

questions.question: Sami asks: 'How is xerostomia treated?' Mina replies:
options: Hydration, saliva substitutes, sialogogues, treatment of the cause
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Treatment is symptomatic and etiological.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will prescribe a saliva substitute.'

questions.question: Sami wonders: 'What is a major aphthous ulcer?' Mina replies:
options: A deep, extensive canker sore, healing with scars
A single, mildly painful canker sore
A canker sore associated with fever
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Major aphthae are deep and leave scars.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will treat with corticosteroids.'

questions.question: Sami asks: 'What is a cold sore?' Mina replies:
options: A recurrent viral infection due to HSV-1, with vesicles on the lips
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Cold sores are a recurrent viral infection.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will prescribe acyclovir.'

questions.question: Sami wonders: 'How is a cold sore treated?' Mina replies:
options: Topical antivirals (acyclovir) or systemic if severe
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Treatment is antiviral.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will prescribe acyclovir cream.'

questions.question: Sami asks: 'What is exfoliative cheilitis?' Mina replies:
options: Desquamation of the lips, often due to trauma, deficiencies, or allergy
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Exfoliative cheilitis has varied causes.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will recommend good hydration.'

questions.question: Sami wonders: 'What is oral pigmentation?' Mina replies:
options: A coloring of the oral mucosa, often benign (melanotic, drug-related)
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Pigmentations have many causes.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will look for signs of malignancy.'

questions.question: Sami asks: 'When should oral melanoma be suspected?' Mina replies:
options: Rapid growth, asymmetry, irregular border, inhomogeneous color
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'The warning criteria are the same as for the skin.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will examine carefully.'

questions.question: Sami wonders: 'What is black hairy tongue?' Mina replies:
options: Hyperkeratosis of the lingual papillae, often due to local factors
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'It's a benign condition.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will recommend good hygiene.'

questions.question: Sami, after facing complex pathologies with Mina, says: 'I am proud of our successes!' Mina concludes: 'Complex pathologies in oral medicine are...'
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Complex pathologies in oral medicine are the key to correct management.' 🦅 Sami: 'I will continue to improve.'
